_comment: Live transcription of the HUMAN leg of the call - the part OpenAI Realtime does not give us
for free, because on that leg nothing is listening. Each browser transcribes its OWN
microphone and posts the finished lines; no audio is stored, by either side, exactly as on the
Everything here is read at request time, so the protocol can be corrected without a rebuild.
That matters more than usual: this was written to the documentation rather than against a
live endpoint, and the first real proof is a pilot call.
model: the Azure DEPLOYMENT name, which is whatever it was called when deployed - not
necessarily the model name. Empty disables transcription entirely and the call runs as before.
participantSide: false transcribes only the agent, which is the agent's own voice and needs no
further ethics consideration. true also transcribes the participant on the human leg -
defensible, since their audio already reaches the same Azure resource on the AI leg, but check
how the ethics application words it before turning it on.
